newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PZU insurer Jan-Sept net down to PLN 38 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish PZU insurer Jan-Sept net down to PLN 38 mln.

text.p: Poland's largest insurer, state- owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), netted 37.9 million zlotys in the first three quarters of this year, about half of the result for the same period of 1995, PZU's deputy president said.
Elzbieta Turkowska-Tyrluk told a news conference the pre-tax profit was 49.6 million zlotys, down 32 percent in the same period last year. @
She said that in the first three quarters of this year PZU collected about 2.7 billion zlotys in gross premiums, 50 percent above 1.82 billion zlotys collected over the same period last year.
"This is 114 percent of our plan for the three quarters and 94 percent of our 1996 plan, so this augurs that the gross premiums target will be exceeded," Turkowska-Tyrluk said.
She said total revenues after three quarters amounted to three billion zlotys, with revenues of 200 million zlotys from investments and five million zlotys from reinsurance. @

Turkowska-Tyrluk said treasury bonds accounted for 70 percent of PZU's investment portfolio, T-bills had a 22 percent share and shares of listed companies accounted for six percent of PZU's investments.
PZU, a virtual monopolist before the fall of communism in 1989, is slated for privatisation, which its management wants to see started in the first quarter of next year.
PZU had a net profit of 105.2 million zlotys on gross premiums of 2.2 billion zlotys in 1995.
It netted 52 million zlotys in the first half of 1996.
